title: Range Rover Sport Electric özellikleri ve menzili açıklandı
summary: Land Rover'ın elektrikli ailesine katılan yeni Range Rover Sport Electric, 118,5 kWh bataryasıyla WLTP standardında yaklaşık 378 mil menzil sunuyor.
body:
JLR, elektrikli SUV ailesini Range Rover Sport Electric modeliyle genişletti. Şirketin açıklamasına göre yeni Range Rover Sport Electric, daha büyük kardeşiyle aynı altyapıyı paylaşmasına rağmen daha erişilebilir bir fiyat etiketi ve farklı bir sürüş ayarıyla geliyor. İki elektrikli motora sahip olan lüks model, 550 beygire varan güç üretirken 0'dan 60 mile 4,3 saniyede ulaşabiliyor.

## Teknik özellikler ve şarj kapasitesi

118,5 kilowatt-saat kapasiteli devasa bir bataryayla donatılan araç, WLTP standardında 378 mile varan bir menzil sunuyor. 800 voltluk mimari sayesinde SUV, uygun koşullarda 10 dakikada 136 mil menzil kazanabiliyor ve yüzde 10'dan yüzde 80 doluluğa 22 dakikada ulaşıyor. WIRED ve InsideEVs'in aktardığına göre, bu performans odaklı model markanın bugüne kadarki en sert gövde yapısına ve en düşük ağırlık merkezine sahip Range Rover Sport versiyonu olarak öne çıkıyor. Ayrıca araç, 900 milimetreye kadar sudan geçebilme ve 45 derecelik eğimleri tırmanabilme gibi gelişmiş arazi yeteneklerini de koruyor.

## Rekabet ve satış planları

## Fiyatlandırma

Porsche Cayenne Electric, BMW iX xDrive60 ve Lucid Gravity gibi iddialı elektrikli modellerle rekabet edecek olan Range Rover Sport Electric, WIRED'ın haberine göre İngiltere'de 109.810 sterlinden başlayan fiyatlarla satışa çıkacak. InsideEVs'in şirket temsilcisine dayandırdığı bilgiye göre ise araç, 2027 modeli olarak ABD pazarına gelmeyecek ancak gelecekte bu pazarda yer alabileceği belirtiliyor.

**Neden önemli?** Markanın amiral gemisi elektrikli modeline kıyasla daha uygun fiyatlı bir alternatif sunan bu yeni lüks SUV, JLR'ın elektrik dönüşüm stratejisinde kritik bir rol oynuyor.

source_texts.title: Range Rover Sport Electric: Price, Specs, Availability
source_texts.summary: By sharing the same platform, the Sport gets the same specs as the classier Range Rover Electric, but with added torque at a smaller outlay.
source_texts.text:
Sandwiched between the launch of the long-awaited full-fat Range Rover Electric at the start of September and the upcoming final reveal of the much-anticipated Jaguar Type 01 in New York City next week, comes—with considerably less fanfare—JLR's Range Rover Sport Electric.
However, considering that Range Rover Sport sales often run close to, or occasionally slightly higher than, the flagship Range Rover, thanks in part to its lower price, this all-electric version of the Sport could be just as important for an embattled JLR. The automaker announced earlier this month that it is cutting 4,000 jobs over the next two years.
According to JLR, the performance SUV has the stiffest body (unsurprising, considering the battery placement) and lowest center of gravity of any Range Rover Sport model, as well as a faster torque response than the Range Rover Electric—50 percent faster, apparently.
Crucially, the Sport gets the same powertrain as the Range Rover, but at a lower price (from £109,810, no US prices yet) and with different tuning. Like its larger sibling, the two 260-kilowatt motors dish out up to 550 pferdestärke (PS) and 850 Newton-meters (Nm) of torque (more than any other Range Rover Sport to date). It can go from standstill to 60 mph in 4.3 seconds if you're in the EV's Dynamic Launch Mode.
As for range, Range Rover claims the Sport with its 118.5-kilowatt-hour battery will get up to 374 miles on the WLTP standard, which should mean about 320 miles under the EPA's stricter testing. Split-charging tech and an 800-volt architecture let the SUV add 136 miles of range in as little as 10 minutes in ideal charging conditions, and go from 10 to 80 percent in 22 minutes.
For dynamic driving as well as off-road smarts, the Sport has all-wheel steering and electronic Active Roll Control, which can supposedly apply up to 1,400 Nm of force across each axle to keep “maximum composure,” as well as an adaptive dynamics system that monitors 100 parameters 500 times per second for greater control of body roll and pitch when cornering or braking. The car can also wade through up to 900 mm of water and tackle 45-degree inclines.
As a last flourish, an “aerodynamically-optimized” grille and alloy wheels supposedly contribute up to 10 extra miles of driving range at motorway speeds.
JLR will produce Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV), gas, and diesel versions of the Sport, but the electric model will go toe to toe with the likes of the Porsche Cayenne Electric, BMW iX xDrive60, and Lotus Eletre 600. The Porsche starts £20,000 cheaper than the Sport, though.
The Polestar 3 Dual Motor is another competitor to the Sport Electric, but not in the US, as Polestar was banned from selling its cars earlier this year because the brand is majority Chinese-owned. The ruling made Polestar the first major casualty of a US rule banning Chinese software in new internet-connected vehicles.

source_texts.title: The Range Rover Sport Electric Is Here To Take On The Lucid Gravity
source_texts.summary: The popular SUV is getting the same electric treatment as its bigger brother, with 350 kW charging and roughly 400 miles of range.
source_texts.text:
The Range Rover Sport Electric Is Here To Take On The Lucid Gravity
The popular SUV is getting the same electric treatment as its bigger brother, with 350 kW charging and roughly 400 miles of range.
- One of the most important cars in Land Rover’s portfolio is going electric.
- The new Range Rover Sport Electric looks identical to its gas-powered sibling.
- It’s based on the same underpinnings as the big Range Rover Electric.
The Range Rover Sport has always been the go-to British car for everyone who wants a luxurious, good-to-drive SUV without having to shell out the money for the big Range Rover. And now, there’s an all-electric RRS, which borrows all of its big brother’s underpinnings, including the massive 118.5-kilowatt-hour battery.
Land Rover, the marque’s parent company, says the huge 800-volt pack enables a WLTP-rated 378 miles (609 kilometers) of range on a full charge, a minor upgrade over the 373-mile (600 km) range of its larger counterpart. That’s because the Sport has always been slightly smaller and lighter than the big daddy.
Range Rover Sport Electric
That puts it clearly in Lucid Gravity territory, where the American electric SUV is currently a best buy, with a whopping 450-mile range, courtesy of a 123-kWh battery pack. The Gravity can also charge wickedly fast, at up to 400 kilowatts, adding roughly 200 miles of range in as little as 11 minutes. What’s more, Lucid’s flagship SUV can accommodate up to seven adults, whereas the RRS is a five-seater only.
Both SUVs are roughly the same size, but given Land Rover's extensive experience in making capable off-roaders, the new RRS EV should leave most of its competitors in the dust—if owners dare to leave paved roads.
Land Rover’s latest electric SUV can charge at up to 350 kilowatts, with a 10-to-80% session taking 22 minutes at a powerful enough DC fast charger. On AC charging, the Range Rover Sport Electric can accept up to 22 kW.
Based on the same MLA architecture as the Range Rover Electric, the new RRS EV shares the same 118-inch (2,997-millimeter) wheelbase as its bigger brother, though its total length is 194.7 inches (4,946 mm), 4.2 inches less than the brand’s flagship.
Range Rover Sport Electric
Motivation is provided by two individual electric motors, each rated at 349 horsepower. Combined, the all-wheel-drive setup provides 542 hp and a healthy 627 pound-feet of torque, just like the Range Rover Electric, which is enough to propel the new Sport from a standstill to 62 miles per hour (0-100 kilometers per hour) in 4.3 seconds. That’s 0.2 seconds faster than the big Rangie and half a second quicker than the top-spec gas-powered Range Rover Sport SV.
Earlier this year, Land Rover said that its Sport-branded EV will also be available with a slightly less powerful 444 hp setup, while keeping the dual-motor all-wheel drive configuration. Now, though, the top-spec model is the only one offered, in a strategy that seems heavily inspired by Porsche’s moves.
Despite the silent, instant-torque powertrain, the new Range Rover Sport Electric retains the gas model’s looks, both inside and out. That’s not exactly a bad thing, seeing how all Range Rovers are quite elegant, but it’s certainly the exact opposite of what Jaguar has done with its electric rebranding.
And now for a piece of bad news. The Range Rover Sport Electric is not coming to the United States as a 2027 model, a company representative told InsideEVs. That said, the model may make an appearance stateside later down the road, possibly as a 2028 model. When that happens, the RRS EV will join its gas-powered siblings, which are available with either a 3.0-liter six-cylinder, a plug-in hybrid, or a 4.4-liter V-8 lump.
Pricing hasn't been announced yet, but it's bound to be more affordable than the $140,450 Range Rover Electric.
